# Build decisions

Decisions made during the build, recorded so later work and reviewers can see why the implementation differs from, or adds to, the [numbered specifications](../notes/files/00_index.md). Deployment-specific values (addresses, secrets, account IDs) are kept in an untracked local file, not here.

Status: **Confirmed** by the owner, or **Build default** chosen during implementation and open to change.

## Scope additions and changes

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | **Quick chat**: temporary Simon conversations not attached to a task. Floating button at the bottom right, shown only when no task is selected; the panel opens out of the button; full screen on mobile. Ending the chat deletes it; unattended chats expire after 24 hours; "Save as task" turns it into a task that keeps the conversation. Simon acts as a workspace helper (find/open/create/move tasks, reminders, drafting, approved connector actions, handoff prompts) and can read but not edit a named task. No Vault or incoming MCP access; not searchable. | Confirmed | New note 18 and screen brief |
| D2 | **Six themes**: Studio, Paper, Pebble, Postcard, Meadow and Tide from the UI sample, each usable with any accent and Light/Dark/System. | Confirmed | Note 02 and themes brief (four themes) |
| D3 | **Reminders are due-date notices, not alarms**: delivered at the top of the hour in the user's local time. The scanner wakes at :00, :15 and :30 past each UTC hour, which gives every current IANA zone its local top of the hour (covers +5:30, +5:45, +8:45, +12:45/+13:45, −3:30 and −9:30; no zone needs :45). Reminder times are whole hours; relative reminders round down; snooze offers 1 hour, Tomorrow at 9 and a custom hour. | Confirmed (timing); build default (mechanism, choices) | Note 15 (60 s polling, 15-minute snooze) |
| D4 | **Incoming MCP** at `/mcp` on the API origin, authenticated by **OAuth 2.1** (with an in-app consent screen) and by **bearer API keys**. | Confirmed | Agent connections brief (auth pending) |
| D5 | **Analytics on, with a mandatory cookie consent banner**. Nothing loads or is stored before Accept; Decline is as easy as Accept; the choice syncs with Settings → Account → Privacy. The banner appears after sign-in because login, Vault and share routes never load analytics. PostHog US cloud. | Confirmed | Note 17 (settings-only opt-in) |
| D6 | **All Composio connectors** are offered, fetched live from Composio on demand and not stored. Auth configs are looked up or created automatically. Connectors that cannot use shared credentials are hidden unless the user can supply their own API key through Composio's hosted form. | Confirmed (catalogue); build default (hiding) | Onboarding/connections briefs (sample catalogue) |
| D7 | **Composio-managed shared OAuth** until a business case is proven. Switching to own OAuth apps later requires affected users to reconnect, surfaced as Needs attention. | Confirmed | Note 12 |
| D8 | **AI providers**: OpenAI by default (Fast `gpt-5.6-luna`, Smart `gpt-5.6-terra`, verified on OpenAI's model pages on 2026-09-15). Provider registry also supports Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic), Google Vertex AI and Together AI. OpenAI programmatic tool calling (hosted code runtime) is never enabled. AI operational telemetry is on (no content). | Confirmed | Note 07 |

## Architecture and operations

| # | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | `DURABLE=true` in hosted environments. Local development without a Trigger secret key falls back to the Nest executor, which the spec already supports. | Confirmed |
| A2 | Hosting: Next.js on Vercel, NestJS on Render (single always-on instance), Trigger.dev Cloud. Merges to `main` auto-deploy all three. Vercel previews run without a backend until a separate dev backend exists, so previews never reach production. | Confirmed (hosting, auto-deploy); build default (previews) |
| A3 | Trigger machines: **micro** for most tasks including chat runs; **small-1x** for Git document tasks. On out-of-memory, idempotent background tasks retry on a larger machine; chat runs are marked interrupted with an explicit Retry, never re-run automatically. | Confirmed (sizes); build default (OOM handling) |
| A4 | Master keys (`CONTENT_KEK`, `VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY`) come from environment variables behind a key-provider interface so a KMS can be enabled later without code changes. | Confirmed |
| A5 | Runtime and tooling verified 2026-09-15: Node.js 24 LTS (24.21.0 current; `engines` >=24.15), pnpm 12.4.2, Trigger.dev 4.6.0 (`runtime: "node-24"`, Git via `aptGet`). Remaining stack versions are recorded in [progress](progress.md) as they are verified. | Build default |
| A6 | pnpm 12 supply-chain policy is kept: dependency build scripts are allowed only for listed packages, and deliberately pinned releases newer than the minimum release age are listed explicitly in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. | Build default |
| A7 | **Local development adapters**: without Cloudflare/Resend/AI credentials the app runs locally with clearly labeled development adapters (SQLite file standing in for D1 with the same batch semantics, filesystem standing in for R2, OTP emails printed to the server log). They are refused when `NODE_ENV=production`. Production uses D1 REST and R2 only. | Build default |
| A8 | Every feature ships with tests. Integrations are tested against stand-ins that model documented provider behavior, plus separately labeled live checks that run only when credentials are present. | Confirmed |

## Architecture review 1 rulings

Build defaults recorded when architecture review 1 (`docs/build/reviews/architecture-review-1.md`) was applied to the [architecture](architecture.md). Each row changes or interprets a specification.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | **Vault unlock runs server-side.** The api derives the passphrase key with Argon2id and issues a `__Host-sym_vault` session bound to the user and login session (5 minutes idle, 60 minutes absolute). The passphrase exists only in request memory: never logged, never in error reports or idempotency records. Unlock allows 5 failures per 15 minutes then a 15-minute lockout, and 20 per 24 hours, counted in D1. Simon grants name one item, task, tool slug and argument path, last at most 24 hours, and resolved values are redacted from results. | Build default | Note 05 ("unlock locally", "regular vault decryption can remain in the browser") |
| R2 | **Encrypted worker-to-api push is the only durable output path.** The worker posts signed, encrypted chunk envelopes to the api. No Trigger realtime streams, `chat.agent`, `AgentChat` or transcript storage, no `@ai-sdk/otel` (`TRIGGER_AI_SDK_OTEL_AUTOREGISTER=0`, AI SDK telemetry off), a redacting worker logger, and ids-only Trigger payloads, metadata, outputs and tags, verified by a marker-string test. | Build default | Note 07 (Trigger session output consumed by Nest); Trigger research recommendations for `chat.agent` and streams |
| R3 | **D1 budget allocation and a dedicated worker token.** All runtimes together stay at or below 3 requests per second: api 2 req/s (burst 10, unauthenticated work at most 30%), worker at most 1 req/s in total through its own D1 token, a bounded D1 queue family and per-process token buckets. Any 429 opens a process-wide circuit for Retry-After (default 300 s). The live suite must confirm whether Cloudflare limits apply per token, user or account; the owner should request a limit increase before a wider beta. | Build default | Note 07 gap 2 (handle rate limits); Cloudflare research R1 |
| R4 | **Symplist-owned single-approval pauses.** `parallelToolCalls: false`; an `execute_tools` call holds either only approval-exempt actions or exactly one approval-requiring action, so each pause has one approval. Decisions are approve (optionally with edited arguments that create a fresh review and digest), deny or dismiss, each applied by one owner-bound conditional statement so exactly one decision per approval takes effect; denial, dismissal and time-based or connection-change expiry go back to the model in a continuation, while restriction and task archive stop the paused run without one. A pending approval or question keeps the conversation active for queueing, and a chat reply is never an approval. The approval policy is deterministic. | Build default | Note 12 (per-action approval inside batches); AI SDK research (SDK `toolApproval`) |
| R5 | **Per-user Composio session** pinned to connected accounts confirmed through a Symplist connection attempt (nonce, same login session, callback identity verification). `manage_connections` is a native Symplist tool that never calls `COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS`. | Build default | Note 12 (`manage_connections` mapping); Composio research (session per chat) |
| R6 | **Git runs in a `document-git` task** (small-1x, awaited by the chat run) in durable mode and in process locally; it never runs inside the chat run. Every publication writes an immutable encrypted head snapshot, which serves outline, section reads, changes, search indexing and artifact snapshots. | Build default | Note 11 (runtime and Git operations); A3 |
| R7 | **Editor formatting normalization and section-level view switching.** The first page-view edit of a non-canonical document publishes a separate "Formatting normalized" commit treated as content-neutral; documents with raw HTML open read-only in the page view; switching between page and raw views preserves the section, not the character position. | Build default | Note 11 (autosave); task document brief ("switching views preserves content and position") |
| R8 | **Proceeding without live D1 verification.** The owner instructed the build not to wait for Cloudflare credentials, so feature waves build against conservative local semantics (string params, same-batch verification `SELECT`, `STRICT` tables). The live D1 suite runs as soon as credentials exist and any divergence is fixed before beta. | Build default | Note 04 (demonstrate atomic REST design); research requirement to verify before building |
| R9 | **`analytics_id` and consent state are plaintext operational metadata.** The id is random and never exposed in responses or logs; server emitters read it without decryption, and account purge must read it after the account key is shredded. | Build default | Note 17 ("account-side protected mapping") |
| R10 | **Expand-only migrations with a CI `migrate` job** that runs before the Trigger deploy; Render pre-deploy runs the same idempotent runner as a safety net. Contract changes ship a release later, and merged migration files never change. | Build default | Hosting decision A2 (independent auto-deploys) |
| R11 | **One-time secrets are never replayable.** Invite codes, API keys, share tokens and OAuth codes appear only in the minting response; idempotency records keep a redacted outcome, and retries return `secretUnavailable: true` with a revoke-and-replace path. | Build default | Notes 04 and 16 (show once) |
| R12 | **Account deletion is an immediate crypto-shred** (deleting the account key row in the same batch as the restriction), followed by an idempotent purge of Composio accounts (revoked upstream), R2 objects, D1 rows and PostHog data. Residual window: D1 Time Travel retains prior states for 30 days; R2 is unversioned; Trigger holds no content (decision R2); PostHog deletion is asynchronous. | Build default | P4; settings account brief (deletion process) |
| R13 | **Admin bootstrap runs once**, only while no admin and no bootstrap event exist, and never clears suspension or relock; re-bootstrapping needs an explicit forced CLI run with actor and reason. | Build default | Note 04 (bootstrap first administrator) |

## Product behavior defaults (task_actions, archive, calendar briefs)

| # | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Completing a parent with open subtasks asks first: Complete all, Only the parent, or Cancel. | Confirmed |
| P2 | Restoring an archived task returns it to its original collection, falling back to Now. | Confirmed |
| P3 | Moving a subtask to another collection makes it a top-level task there, with Undo. | Confirmed |
| P4 | No hard delete of tasks in beta; archive only. Account deletion is the only deletion path. | Confirmed |

## Foundation build defaults

Decisions made while building the foundation (Phase C) against the [architecture](architecture.md), each verified in the repository on 2026-09-15.

| # | Decision | Status | Supersedes / extends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | **Relative imports use `.ts` specifiers.** `tsconfig.base.json` sets `allowImportingTsExtensions` and `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`, so `tsc -b` emits `.js` specifiers in `dist` while Turbopack, Vitest and the Trigger bundler read sources directly. Turbopack in Next 16.3.5 cannot resolve NodeNext `.js` specifiers to `.ts` files (a `next build` importing `@symplist/contracts` through `turbopack.resolveAlias` failed with 52 "Module not found" errors). A structural test rejects `.js` relative specifiers in `packages/*/src` and `apps/api/src`. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (6) |
| F2 | **Vitest resolves `@symplist/*` through a resolver plugin, not `resolve.conditions`.** The shared config maps each workspace specifier to its package's `source` export. Vitest forwards `ssr.resolve.conditions` to test workers as Node `--conditions` flags, and third-party packages also publish a `source` export (for example `eventsource`, loaded by `@trigger.dev/core`) that points at TypeScript files Node refuses to load from `node_modules`, so a test importing `queue` from `@trigger.dev/sdk` crashed with the conditions approach. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (4) |
| F3 | **`vitest.config.ts` files import the shared config by relative path** (`packages/testing/src/vitest-config.ts`). Vite's config loader resolves bare imports with only the `node` condition, so importing `@symplist/testing/vitest` there would require a built `dist`. `@symplist/testing` depends on the packages whose interfaces its fakes and contract suites cover (config, contracts, crypto, db, email, storage); those packages never depend on it, so the workspace graph stays acyclic. Every other package and app lists it as a dev dependency. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (4), §17 |
| F4 | **Two tsconfigs per built project.** `tsconfig.json` is the composite build (tests excluded, `tsBuildInfoFile` inside `dist` so deleting `dist` gives a clean build); `tsconfig.typecheck.json` is the `noEmit` check with `customConditions: ["source"]` that includes tests and `vitest.config.ts`. The web typecheck runs `next typegen` first, and `next-env.d.ts` is not committed. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (1), (3) |
| F5 | **`pnpm build` runs `next build` before `tsc -b`**, so the CI build step is also the clean-clone web build smoke test (no package `dist` exists yet). `pnpm build:web:clean` removes `packages/*/dist` and builds the web app for the same check locally. A web test asserts that the Turbopack aliases are exactly the browser-safe entries and match each package's `source` export, and a static import scan in `packages/testing` keeps those entries free of `node:*` and server-only workspace imports. | Build default | Architecture §2 and §2.2 (6) |
| F6 | **Pins not spelled out in the stack lock:** `@tanstack/react-query` 5.102.8 (latest stable on 2026-09-15); `cn` 0.3.0 in `apps/web` (installed by `shadcn init` 4.21.0 and re-exported by its generated `lib/utils.ts`); `react-dom` 19.3.0 in `packages/email` (required peer of `react-email` and `@react-email/render`); `zod` 4.6.5 in the worker, agent, integrations and analytics packages (required peer of `@trigger.dev/sdk`, `ai` and `@composio/core`). `shadcn` is a web dependency as `init` makes it. It brings `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.0 in as its own transitive dependency, as the `trigger.dev` CLI already did; Symplist code never imports it (the MCP server uses the 2.0 packages). | Build default | Architecture §1 |
| F7 | **`core-js: false` in `allowBuilds`.** It arrives through `posthog-js`, and its postinstall only prints a funding message. | Build default | A6 |
| F8 | **Error-code maps map each code to its HTTP status**, declared per feature with `defineErrorCodes` and composed in the contracts index; a test fails if two owners declare the same code, event type or tool name. Common codes: `not_found` 404, `rate.limited` 503 and `idempotency.mismatch` 422 (the status the IETF Idempotency-Key draft uses for a reused key with a different payload). | Build default | Architecture §6, §6.1 |
| F9 | **`@symplist/core` exports one subpath per core domain** (`@symplist/core/access`, `@symplist/core/events`, …) and re-exports each domain as a namespace from its root, so domain builders never edit the manifest and names never collide. | Build default | Architecture §2.2 (1), §2.3 |
| F10 | **Nest decorator transform in tests is configured explicitly** (`oxc.decorator: { legacy: true, emitDecoratorMetadata: true }` in `apps/api/vitest.config.ts`), because Oxc takes these options from the tsconfig that includes a file and the build tsconfig excludes tests. The api test asserts `design:paramtypes` for `HealthController`. | Build default | Architecture §17 |
| C1.1 | **Ids accept only canonical lowercase UUIDv7 text**, branded per entity (`TaskId`, `RunId`, …) with `brandedIdSchema`, so one id never has two spellings in D1 rows, R2 keys or cache keys. Request ids stay opaque tokens (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`). | Build default | Architecture §3.4 |
| C1.2 | **Foundation error codes:** `validation` 400, `internal` 500, `auth.session_required` 401, `auth.origin_forbidden` and `auth.csrf_invalid` 403, `access.unverified`, `access.locked`, `access.relocked`, `access.suspended` and `access.admin_required` 403, `idempotency.key_required` and `idempotency.key_invalid` 400, `idempotency.in_progress` 409, `task.archived` and `task.run_active` 409, besides F8's codes. `rate.limited` carries `details.retryAfter` in whole seconds (1 to 86400); `validation` details carry path, code and a fixed message, never the input. `defineErrorCodes`, `defineEvents` and `defineTools` reject malformed names at import. | Build default | Architecture §6, §6.1; F8 |
| C1.3 | **One-time secret responses are a strict union on `secretUnavailable`:** the minting response carries the secret fields with `secretUnavailable: false`; an exact retry carries only the non-secret fields with `secretUnavailable: true` and `notice: "secret.already_issued"`, and can never carry a secret field. | Build default | Architecture §6.1; R11 |
| C1.4 | **WebSocket frame contracts:** user-topic events (the §7 list, each owned by one feature in `userTopicEventOwners`) travel only on `user`, every other event only on `conversation:<id>`; the composed decoder rejects unknown event types; malformed client frames are answered with `{"t":"err","code":"validation"}`. `openTasks` must be unique; the user snapshot's `heads` holds at most 20 opaque revisions. | Build default | Architecture §7 |
| C1.5 | **Environment parsing:** an empty value counts as unset; booleans accept only `true`/`false` and `LIVE_*` only `1`/`0`; integers must be canonical decimals; origins must be canonical (`scheme://host[:port]`, no path or trailing slash), including `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL`. `NODE_ENV` is required on the api and defaults to `production` on the worker (Trigger.dev images set `production`, `trigger dev` sets `development`), so `WorkerConfig` gains `NODE_ENV`. Defaults: `PORT` 4000, `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` 0 outside production, OTP 6 digits/10 minutes/5 attempts, Vault idle 5 minutes, lateness and quick-chat TTL 24 hours, `DOC_MAX_BYTES` 1 MiB (also the maximum, so an encrypted draft fits D1's 2 MB value limit), `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` UTC, `GIT_TMP_DIR` `<os tmpdir>/symplist-git`, AI tiers from D8, `AI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` true (D8), `BETA_ACCESS_REQUIRED`, reminders and AI true, analytics false. | Build default | Architecture §16.1, §16.2 |
| C1.6 | **Cross-field rules added to §16.1:** production also requires https/wss origins, `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` and `AI_PROVIDER_MODE=live` (scripted stays allowed in development and test); `WS_ORIGIN` must share `API_ORIGIN`'s host and port; `ARTIFACT_ORIGIN` must use a different hostname from `API_ORIGIN` and `WEB_ORIGIN`; the api needs `EMAIL_FROM_REMINDERS` when `DURABLE=false`; analytics with a project key needs `POSTHOG_HOST`, and on the api `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY` and `POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID` so account deletion can delete PostHog data; Bedrock and Vertex credentials must be complete groups. Missing AI credentials never fail startup (`ai.unavailable`). | Build default | Architecture §5.6, §5.8, §13, §16.1 |
| C1.7 | **Secret inventory enforcement:** a "no" cell (`TRIGGER_ACCESS_TOKEN` on api and worker) is refused like "rejected"; with `DURABLE=true` the api refuses the secret AI credentials (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `GOOGLE_VERTEX_CREDENTIALS_JSON`, `TOGETHER_API_KEY`) but not region, project or location; the worker patterns also match unversioned names (`VAULT_RECOVERY_KEY`); an unversioned family name is refused in every runtime. The web config refuses every inventory secret and any `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` outside the four public names, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` must be a `phc_` project key; http/ws web URLs are allowed only for loopback hosts, because the e2e suite runs a production web build against a local api. | Build default | Architecture §4.5, §16.1 |
| C1.8 | **`syncEnvVars` source:** `workerSyncEnvVars(process.env)` from `@symplist/config/worker` selects only the allowlist (every worker variable except `NODE_ENV` and `TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY`, plus the worker families' `<NAME>_<n>` and `<NAME>_CURRENT`), always syncs `TRIGGER_AI_SDK_OTEL_AUTOREGISTER=0`, marks provider credentials and family versions secret, and validates the selection with the worker schema before returning it, so a deploy fails instead of syncing an invalid or forbidden configuration. | Build default | Architecture §4.5, §8.8 |
| C1.9 | **`pnpm secrets:generate` imports the inventory** from `packages/config/src/secrets.ts` through Node 24 type stripping (the file is dependency-free and uses only erasable syntax), prints shared families first and api-only families under a separate heading, takes no arguments and never writes files. The browser-safe scan also fails entries that reach `posthog-node`, `@aws-sdk/*`, `@composio/core`, `resend`, `@nestjs/*`, `@trigger.dev/*`, the MCP server packages, Express middleware and the AI SDK provider packages. | Build default | Architecture §2, §16.3 |
| CR1 | **Envelope key versions are data key versions.** The `<keyVersion>` of `sym1` envelopes, the object header `kv` and the AAD `k` name the version of the data key that encrypted them (the account data key, or the Vault data key for items). Each account and Vault has one data key, so every envelope in this format generation carries `1`, and decryption rejects any other version with `crypto.unsupported_key_version` before touching the ciphertext (so the version is never malleable, even in the Vault item and grant AADs that omit `k`). `CONTENT_KEK` rotation unwraps the account key with its recorded KEK version and re-wraps it under the current one (`rewrapAccountKey`); envelopes are never re-encrypted. A later data-key rotation adds versions without changing the formats. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2 |
| CR2 | **Key wrap and object layout details.** Every `symk1` wrap (account key, Vault passphrase, recovery and session) and the object `wk` is base64url of 12-byte IV, 32-byte encrypted key and 16-byte tag (80 characters). The per-object key is wrapped by the account data key under the same object AAD as the body (different keys). The object header is canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) `{"alg":"A256GCM","iv","kv","v","wk"}` after `SYMO`, version byte `1` and a big-endian uint32 header length; `v` is the object format version from the caller, and non-canonical headers are rejected. HKDF-SHA256 uses an empty salt and only the five fixed labels; the Vault session HKDF input is the token's 32 raw bytes. Random bytes are drawn in a fixed order (data key or object key, then wrap IV, then body IV) so the committed vectors in `packages/crypto/test-vectors/v1.json` are reproducible. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §11.1 |
| CR3 | **AAD encoder rules and the run chunk and idempotency bindings.** AAD field names are `a`–`z`; values are non-empty strings of at most 1,024 UTF-16 units without lone surrogates (escaped exactly as `JSON.stringify` does) or non-negative safe integers; `f` must be `sym1`, `symo1` or `symk1` and `p` is required. Run chunks bind purpose `run_chunk`, table `runs`, row = run id, column `seq:<seq>`. Idempotency responses bind purpose `idempotency_response`, owner = the record's user, table `idempotency_records`, row = canonical JSON `[scope, key]` (unambiguous when either contains separators) and column `response_enc`. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §4.2, §6.1 |
| CR4 | **Crypto size limits.** Field (`sym1`) plaintext at most 1 MiB, so an envelope stays under D1's 2 MB value limit; object plaintext at most 256 MiB; object header at most 1 KiB; digest input at most 16 MiB; Argon2id secrets at most 4 KiB of UTF-8. Tokens are 16 to 1,024 bytes (32 by default); OTPs are 6 to 12 digits drawn with one uniform `crypto.randomInt` call. Oversized input fails with `crypto.input_too_large`. | Build default | Architecture §4.1, §5.1 |
| CR5 | **Digest value encodings.** Each §4.3 purpose is accepted only with its own secret family. The OTP digest value is canonical JSON `[challengeId, purpose, code]`. Idempotency fingerprints and approval argument digests hash canonical JSON (keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, `JSON.stringify` scalars, `undefined` object members omitted; non-finite numbers, lone surrogates and non-plain objects rejected); the approval value is `{arguments, connectedAccountId, toolSlug}` and its digest is a bare base64url string because `approvals.arg_digest` stores no version. `email-suppression` digests carry the `CONTENT_KEK` version. A stored digest whose secret version is no longer configured verifies false. Internal event signatures (§6.2) are built by their owner from the exported `hmacSha256` and `constantTimeEqual`. | Build default | Architecture §4.3, §5.1, §6.1, §8.4 |
| CR6 | **Argon2id records and normalization.** Stored records must match the single supported parameter set exactly (`v` 1, `argon2id`, m=19456, t=2, p=1, 16-byte salt, 32-byte hash); anything else fails with `crypto.invalid_password_hash` before any work, so stored data can neither weaken nor inflate the cost. Secrets are NFKC-normalized before hashing (NIST SP 800-63B), so composed and decomposed input verify alike. Vault key derivation takes a salt-and-parameters record without `hash` (the foundation stub accepted `Argon2idHash`, which would have stored the wrapping key beside the wrap). A full semaphore refuses with `rate.limited` and `retryAfter` 1 second. | Build default | Architecture §4.3, §11.1, §13.3 |
| CR7 | **Environment key provider.** A family with no `<NAME>_<n>` or `<NAME>_CURRENT` variables is absent (callers list required families); versions must be canonical positive integers up to 999,999,999; values must be exactly 32 bytes of canonical unpadded base64url; `all()` lists versions newest first by number. Errors name the variable but never echo its value, and `destroy()` zeroises every key buffer. Cross-family equality and per-runtime rejection stay in `@symplist/config` (§4.5). | Build default | Architecture §4.5, decision A4 |
| C3-1 | **Query helper strictness.** `sql(text, params)` accepts only strings, `null`/`undefined` (written as `NULL` literals) and string arrays (expanded to `?, ?` lists; an empty array becomes `NULL`). Numbers and booleans must go through `int()`/`bool()`; unused or missing names throw. Both clients reject non-string params, placeholder-count mismatches, named or numbered placeholders, transaction control and multi-statement entries before any request. Errors carry stable codes; SQLite/D1 text is kept only in a non-enumerable `providerMessage`. | Build default | Architecture §3.2 |
| C3-2 | **D1 lane mechanics.** The api lane is a 10-token bucket at 2 req/s; unauthenticated calls also draw from a 3-token sub-bucket at 0.6 req/s, never queue, and are shed with `rate.limited` whenever tokens are short or authenticated work is waiting. Authenticated calls queue FIFO and are refused when the wait would exceed 5 s (api) or 120 s (worker). Clients share one process-wide lane per kind and one process-wide circuit; the circuit also opens until reset when a `Ratelimit` policy reports 10 or fewer requests remaining. Read-only batches retry up to 3 attempts (200 ms base, full jitter, 2 s cap) on retryable D1 messages, 5xx, network errors and malformed success bodies; timeouts are not retried. | Build default | Architecture §3.1 |
| C3-3 | **Foundation schema details beyond the column lists.** Every mutable foundation table has `write_id TEXT NOT NULL` (including `user_preferences`, whose §10.3 list omits it). Owner-scoped foundation tables reference `users(id)`; `tasks` has a composite `(parent_id, owner_id)` foreign key to `(id, owner_id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so parents stay in the owner's tree. `beta_admin_events`, `dispatch_intents`, `account_deletions` and `account_tombstones` have no foreign keys because they outlive the users row. `dispatch_intents.kind` and `beta_admin_events.action` are format-checked slugs rather than enums so later features add values without a table rebuild; intents are unique per `(kind, subject_id)`. `otp_challenges` allows one live challenge per user and purpose (partial unique index) and binds `vault_reset`/`account_delete` challenges to an auth session. `executor_state` is seeded with generation 1 and `mode` NULL, recorded by the first api start. `user_preferences` keeps the column name `"group"`, always quoted. | Build default | Architecture §2.1, §3.4, §5.1, §5.6, §8.1, §10.3 |
| C3-4 | **Migration CLI and merged-file check.** `pnpm db:migrate` runs `packages/db/src/cli/migrate.ts` with Node type stripping (the db tsconfigs set `erasableSyntaxOnly`), reads `DATA_DRIVER` or `--driver` (required, no default), prefers `CLOUDFLARE_D1_MIGRATE_API_TOKEN` over `CLOUDFLARE_D1_API_TOKEN` and never uses the worker token, because `@symplist/config` has no environment loader yet. `d1_migrations` keeps wrangler's non-STRICT definition. `scripts/check-migrations.mjs` fails on a modified merged file and on a deleted one when the merge base shows the branch had it; CI fetches `main` (unshallowing) with `GITHUB_TOKEN` passed through git's environment config. | Build default | Architecture §3.4 |
| C3-5 | **Object store semantics.** Keys are ASCII letters, digits and `._~-` in non-empty `/`-separated segments (never `.` or `..`, at most 1024 bytes) on every store; metadata keys are lower-case with printable ASCII values up to 8192 bytes; bodies are capped (100 MiB by default) on write and read. A conditional put that finds its own `write-id` reports `created`; a 409 conditional conflict is resolved by `HeadObject` or reported as `storage.conflict`. `list` never returns metadata (R2 does not). The local store keeps each object as a directory holding `body` and a `meta.json` sidecar, staged with `wx` files and committed by one atomic `rename` that fails when the key exists, so body and sidecar appear together; upper-case letters are escaped for case-insensitive filesystems. | Build default | Architecture §1 (R2 rules), decision A7 |
| C3-6 | **Contract suites and fakes live in `packages/testing/src/contracts/{db,storage}`** and the db and storage package tests import them by relative path (those packages cannot depend on `@symplist/testing`). The REST client also runs the DbClient contract over a fake D1 API backed by `node:sqlite`, and the R2 store runs the ObjectStore contract over a local S3 emulator; live suites run only with `LIVE_D1=1`/`LIVE_R2=1` and credentials, and the live D1 part also probes raw JSON number/boolean/null params and whether two tokens share a rate-limit budget. | Build default | Architecture §3.2, §17 |
| C5.1 | **The Resend transport is a first-party `fetch` client typed with the `resend` package's own types**, not `resend.emails.send`. The SDK reads the global `fetch` (no injection for tests) and `console.error`s full provider error bodies whenever `NODE_ENV` is not `production`, which can echo recipient addresses. The transport sends `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Idempotency-Key` and `User-Agent` to `POST /emails`, maps 400/404/405/422/451 to `email.rejected`, 401/403 to `email.unauthorized`, 409 to `email.idempotency_conflict` (`invalid_idempotent_request`, not retryable) or `email.idempotency_in_flight` (retryable), 429 to `email.rate_limited` (retryable) or `email.quota_exceeded`, 5xx and network failures to retryable codes with `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP date), keeps only the enumerated provider error name, and never retries itself. `resend` stays for webhook verification (§12.5). | Build default | Architecture §12.3, research A1 |
| C5.2 | **Email contracts.** `EmailMessage` gains optional `template` (for redacted logs and Resend tags) and `otp` (read only by the log transport). Idempotency keys are `otp/<purpose>/<challengeId>`, `vault-reset-notice/<resetAuthorizationId>` and `reminder/<occurrenceId>/email`. OTP codes never appear in the subject, inbox preview or `<title>`. Plain text is rendered from the same template without hard wrapping. Reminder links: Open task must be on `WEB_ORIGIN` with no query or fragment; the preferences or one-click opt-out link may carry the narrow token and must be on the web or api origin, and a one-click URL also sets `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post`. Opted-in titles are collapsed to one line and capped at 120 characters. HTML snapshots are stored as `*.html.snap` so Biome does not lint rendered email markup. | Build default | Architecture §5.1, §11.2, §12.3; transactional emails brief |
| C5.3 | **Analytics event owners and properties.** Server-owned: `task_created`, `task_completed`, `task_moved`, `reminder_created`, `handoff_prepared`, `artifact_share_created`, `quick_chat_saved` (the api sees every source, Simon and MCP included). Client-owned: `search_used`, `appearance_changed`, `quick_chat_started`. Each wrapper refuses the other side's events. Properties are strict enums or booleans (for example `result_count` buckets `0`, `1-5`, `6-20`, `21+`; `accent` is `preset` or `custom`, never the color), and every event carries `event_version`. Server captures take a UUID `eventId` from the confirmed action, sent as PostHog's `uuid` for deduplication. | Build default | Note 17 (suggested events), architecture §15 |
| C5.4 | **The scrubber goes beyond research C1.** posthog-js 1.433.4 sent the referring search query as `ph_keyword` in `$identify` properties and `$set_once` in the jsdom test, so `ph_*` keys are stripped, as are `title`, `$lib_custom_api_host`, element and pageview-path keys, and any string value that looks like a URL. `before_send` scrubs first and then fails closed: an event is dropped if any non-`$` property other than `token` and `distinct_id` does not match its schema. | Build default | Architecture §15, research C1 |
| C5.5 | **Analytics consent and delivery details.** Excluded route prefixes are `/signin`, `/access`, `/vault`, `/oauth` and `/artifact`. Withdrawal also removes `ph_*` and `__ph_opt_in_out_*` keys from localStorage, not only sessionStorage. The server emitter checks the `analytics_consent` and `analytics_id` the caller already read from D1 for the request (no extra D1 request per event), uses a 1,000-event queue, 2 batch retries and a 3-second bound on worker `captureImmediate`, and never throws. PostHog event-deletion status is polled per person UUID (looked up by distinct id before `bulk_delete`), because `deletion_status` is keyed by `person_uuid`. | Build default | Architecture §3.1, §5.6, §15 |
| C5.6 | **Test support dependencies and fake semantics.** `@symplist/testing` depends on `ai` 7.0.101 (mock model and `simulateReadableStream`), `@ai-sdk/provider` 4.0.14 (stream part types) and `zod` 4.6.5 (the `ai` peer); `@symplist/analytics` adds `jsdom` 30.0.1 for the §15 payload test. The fakes mirror the SDK surfaces structurally rather than importing `@trigger.dev/sdk` or `@composio/core`. `FakeTriggerClient` releases an idempotency key when a run ends `FAILED`, `CRASHED`, `SYSTEM_FAILURE`, `EXPIRED` or `TIMED_OUT` (the SDK's failed statuses) and keeps it for `COMPLETED` and `CANCELED`; `FakeComposioClient` retries 408, 409, 429, 5xx and timeouts on the default client (`maxRetries` 2) and never on `withOptions({ maxRetries: 0 })`. The e2e tsconfig includes `src` so the helpers are typechecked. | Build default | Architecture §1, §8.3, §14.1, §17 |
